papers.title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve
papers.abstract: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori. As an application, we give a construction of the Tate curve in spectral algebraic geometry. This approach lets us produce a lift of the Tate curve to $\mathbb{S}[[q]]$. We furthermore describe how to lift (arithmetic) toric stacks.

papers.title: A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents
papers.abstract: Let $g_x$ be the Balmer-Favi idempotent at a point $x$ of the spectrum of a rigidly-compactly generated tensor triangulated category. We study the equality $\operatorname{Cosupp}(g_x)=\operatorname{gen}(x)$ by expressing $g_x$ as a local dual. We prove the equality for the derived category of a Noetherian scheme and for the stable module category of a finite group scheme over a field of positive characteristic. For $E(n)$-local spectra we express the maps between distinct monochromatic layers of the sphere in terms of the chromatic fracture square. The height-two splitting gives the equality through height two at every prime. For a Noetherian local ring we characterize the Gorenstein property by the form of its closed-point idempotent.

papers.title: Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories
papers.abstract: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports. We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the K\"unneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.

papers.title: Nontrivial Massey products on compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that the bigraded quasi-isomorphism type of the bigraded, bidifferential algebra of forms on a compact K\"ahler manifold generally contains more information than the de Rham cohomology algebra with its real Hodge structure. More precisely, on any closed Riemann surface of genus at least two, there is a nontrivial ABC-Massey product. Furthermore, starting from dimension three, there are simply connected projective manifolds with a nonzero ABC-Massey product of three divisor classes. In particular, compact K\"ahler manifolds are generally not formal in the sense of pluripotential homotopy theory.

papers.title: On the Residue Sequence in Logarithmic Topological Cyclic Homology
papers.abstract: Algebraic K-theory participates in localization sequences, as first established by Quillen. We identify their boundary maps with the \emph{residue} map from logarithmic TC under the cyclotomic trace, resolving a conjecture of Rognes. As a consequence, we obtain e.g. a trace map from the K-theory of periodic complex K-theory to the logarithmic TC of connective complex K-theory. Moreover, we find that there exists a stable infinity-category C such that TC(C) realizes logarithmic TC for specific log structures, such as the natural ones on discrete valuation rings, connective complex K-theory, and truncated Brown--Peterson spectra. This provides evidence for the existence of a category of modules in the context of logarithmic geometry. We conjecture that such a category can be chosen to reflect additional structure on logarithmic TC, and we give evidence for this for discrete valuation rings.

papers.title: Equivariant intersection cohomology of some $4$-dimensional locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds
papers.abstract: Locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds are singular analogues of quasitoric manifolds. In this paper, we study a certain class of four-dimensional locally standard $T^2$-pseudomanifolds over convex polygons. We establish an Orlik-Raymond type classification and study their ordinary and equivariant cohomology, as well as their intersection and equivariant intersection cohomology. We also introduce ring structures on middle-perversity intersection cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology via change of perversity. We show that these rings can be described in terms of the cohomology and equivariant cohomology of associated nonsingular spaces, which are quasitoric manifolds or $S^4$. Furthermore, we give combinatorial descriptions of the equivariant cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology in terms of labelled graphs.

papers.title: Homotopy Classification of Pointed Self-Maps of $\mathbb{RP}^3\#\mathbb{RP}^3$
papers.abstract: We classify pointed self-maps of $M=\mathbb{RP}^{3}\#\mathbb{RP}^{3}$ up to pointed homotopy. Using the universal cover $S^2\times\mathbb R$, we reduce the problem to paths in the sphere mapping space with even or odd endpoint conditions. The evaluation fibration, Whitehead products, and a double-coset calculation determine the resulting secondary invariants. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism split into four families, each in bijection with $\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. Every other realizable endomorphism sends both standard generators to reflections. For each such endomorphism, the realizable multipliers on $\pi_2(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ are precisely the odd integers $d$, and the classes with fixed multiplier are in bijection with $\mathbb Z/|d|\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. We compute an explicit composition law on the double-reflection submonoid and determine the pointed self-homotopy equivalences. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism form a subset $\mathcal{T}$ that is preserved by composition on either side with arbitrary pointed homotopy classes and satisfies $\mathcal{T}^2=\{0\}$, where $0$ is the constant class. For each fixed triple $(m,k,d)$ in the double-reflection case, the $|d|$ classes induce identical homomorphisms on every homotopy group. Thus the secondary invariant detects distinctions invisible to these induced homomorphisms.

papers.title: Representability of Galois extensions
papers.abstract: We study faithful Galois extensions in a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathscr{C}$ by a dualizable $\mathbb{E}_1$-group $G$. We prove that these extensions correspond to colimit-preserving symmetric monoidal functors from $\mathrm{An}^{\mathrm{B}G}$ to $\mathscr{C}$. Under suitable assumptions, we use this correspondence to construct a Galois pro-anima that classifies Galois extensions in $\mathscr{C}$. This generalizes the \'etale fundamental groupoid of commutative rings and Mathew's weak Galois groupoid.

papers.title: An $(\infty,1)$-category of conically smooth stratified bordisms
papers.abstract: To study derived defect topological quantum field theories, we construct an $(\infty,1)$-category of stratified bordisms and sketch its $(\infty,d)$-dimensional analogue. In the first chapters we develop a method for constructing symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories, inspired by Segal spaces but better suited to geometric inputs, which we call interval Segal spaces. Using this framework, we construct the $(\infty,1)$-category of $d$-dimensional smooth manifolds via smooth $\infty$-sheaves thereof, in an attempt to address fibrancy issues present in prior work on this subject. We further equip this category with a symmetric monoidal structure, compute its homotopy 1-category, and extend the construction to manifolds endowed with tangential structures, obtaining the interval Segal space of $d$-dimensional bordisms with tangential structure. To model the stratifications supporting topological defects, we work with conically smooth stratified spaces, a suitably smooth framework for conical stratifications. We define stratified topological manifolds as stratified $\mathcal{B}$-manifolds for a suitable $(\infty,1)$-category of basics $\mathcal{B}$. Using these, we construct an interval Segal space whose objects are compact closed stratified topological $(d-1)$-manifolds and whose 1-morphisms are stratified $d$-dimensional bordisms, and we endow it with a symmetric monoidal structure. We also use tangential structures on conically smooth stratified spaces to formulate a notion of defect labels, aiming toward bordisms with labeled defects in the style of Carqueville et al. Finally, we sketch a higher-dimensional generalization of the interval category to a category of $d$-cubes for $d>1$, conjecturally presenting $(\infty,d)$-categories, and outline how stratified factorization homology may be used to produce derived stratified defect TQFTs.

papers.title: The $J$-Homomorphism From Localising The Cobordism Hypothesis
papers.abstract: Lurie's cobordism hypothesis classifies fully extended framed topological field theories valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ with duals by the $\infty$-groupoid $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$ of fully dualisable objects. This classification results in an $O(n)$-action on $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$, where $O(n)$ acts on the framed bordism category by change of framing. Lurie observed that for a connective spectrum, this action is ``a version of the classical $J$-homomorphism.'' We make this identification explicit: with respect to the right action of $O(n)$ on framings, the $O(n)$-action on the localisation $L(\mathrm{Bord}_n^{\mathrm{fr}}) \simeq S$ is precisely $\ominus J_n$, the inverse of the unstable $J$-homomorphism $J_n \colon O(n) \to \mathrm{GL}_1(S)$. The identification of the action with the unstable $J$-homomorphism in the setting of smooth stacks is due to Grady--Pavlov; we give an independent proof in Lurie's original formulation of the cobordism hypothesis, using the abstract Pontryagin--Thom construction. The sign (i.e.\ whether the action is $J_n$ or $\ominus J_n$) depends on the convention for the $O(n)$-action on framings, and is relevant for $\mathrm{pin}^\pm$ theories and hence for quantum systems with time-reversal symmetry. We compute the induced action on homotopy groups of the sphere spectrum in low degrees, yielding explicit invariants for invertible TFTs in dimensions $1$, $2$, and $3$, and connect these to the Kitaev chain, the framing anomaly, the spin-statistics theorem, and anomaly inflow. We recover the Galatius--Madsen--Tillmann--Weiss theorem as a consequence of the cobordism hypothesis and relate the homotopy fixed-point and mapping-spectrum perspectives on invertible TFTs via the duality between tangential and normal framings.

papers.title: Cyclic Hasse diagrams of manifolds and noncommutative path cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a connected oriented closed manifold of dimension $d\geq 2$, equipped with a regular CW structure, and let $P$ be its face poset. We consider the cyclic Hasse diagram $G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, obtained from the directed Hasse diagram $G_P$ by adding an arrow from each maximal cell to every $0$-cell of $M$. Over an arbitrary field $\mathbb K$, we completely describe the path cohomology algebra $PH^*(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$ in terms of the $\mathbb K$-Betti numbers of $M$. In particular, this algebra is not graded commutative whenever the dimension of $H^*(M)$ over $\mathbb K$ is at least 4. This disproves Grigor'yan's conjecture on graded commutativity. Moreover, as $M$ ranges over connected oriented closed surfaces, the even subalgebras $PH^{\mathrm{even}}(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$, regarded as ungraded associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras, satisfy no common algebraic identity beyond those satisfied by all associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras. These results distinguish GLMY path cohomology from classical cohomology, whose cup product is graded commutative and whose even subalgebra is commutative. As an application, we construct a digraph $G$ for which the K\"unneth formula for the categorical product $G\times G$ fails, answering a question of Pinto negatively and disproving another conjecture of Grigor'yan.

papers.title: An Implementation of the 3-Dimensional Extended Persistent Homology Transform
papers.abstract: The Extended Persistent Homology Transform (XPHT) describes a shape through the extended persistence diagrams of its directional height functions. We present an algorithm for computing a finite directional sample of the three-dimensional XPHT from a triangulated boundary. Our main construction determines essential first-homology pairings by combining an ordered tree-cotree decomposition with evaluation-dual cocycles. The decomposition supplies a homology basis compatible with the height filtration, while the cocycles are used to determine the essential birth-death pairs. Degree-zero persistence and duality determine the remaining boundary diagrams. Under the boundary-reduction hypotheses and with critical-point sign labels, these diagrams yield the extended persistence of the solid. The resulting procedure uses graph constructions and linear algebra over F2 on boundary meshes extracted from three-dimensional binary images.

papers.title: M\"obius Invertibility of Rank Invariants
papers.abstract: One of the best known invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology is the rank invariant, which is subsumed by the generalized rank invariant (GRI), obtained by naturally extending its domain. M\"obius inversion of the GRI not only provides a compact encoding of this invariant but is also useful for clarifying its relationship with other invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology. However, M\"obius inversion of the GRI has been defined only under suitable finiteness conditions on its domain and support. This work studies the extent to which M\"obius inversion can be extended beyond these finiteness conditions. Namely, we formalize the notion of M\"obius invertibility, which captures when M\"obius inversion exists beyond these finiteness conditions, and investigate when the GRI is M\"obius invertible. A central result we establish is that M\"obius invertibility of the GRI is guaranteed for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules when $d\leq 2$, but may fail when $d>2$. Establishing this failure also corrects an error in the existing literature. In response to this higher-dimensional obstruction, we show that for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules, restricting the GRI to intervals subordinate to the finite grid supporting a minimal free presentation preserves its M\"obius inversion whenever the latter exists over all intervals. Since computing the GRI over all intervals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is infeasible in practice, this result provides a principled justification for restricting the GRI to those intervals.

papers.title: Klein four slices of the representation suspensions of $H\underline{\mathbb{F}_2}$
papers.abstract: We study the regular slice filtration of representation spheres $S^V\wedge H\underline{M}$. For every finite group $G$, we locate all slices in an explicit interval $[n(V),k(V)]$ and show that both endpoints occur. We introduce a \emph{defect vector} to measure a slice's failure. For the Klein four-group with $\underline{\mathbb F}_2$-coefficients, a balanced defect allows us to move $S^V\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ by certain $RO(G)$-graded cohomology classes to its $\dim V$-slice, which is again a representation sphere, while an odd defect obstructs any spherical slice. As an application, we obtain closed formulas for the bottom slice of $\Sigma^nH\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$ for every $n$, recovering the computation of Guillou and Yarnall by a different method. Along the way, we determine the complete slice tower of $S^{\infty\alpha_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ and consequently, the partial tower for $S^{n\alpha_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$.

papers.title: A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field. It follows that, in that case, polynomial maps are endowed with an Hopf structure. In a second part, we study non repeated Milnor invariants (in the $4$-dimensional context of $2$-string links) from this pseudo-morphism point of view. We show that they form a sub-bialgebra of the Hopf algebra of pseudo-morphisms on the group of $2$-string links up to link-homotopy, and prove that it is isomorphic to an explicit quotient $\textrm{Mil}$ of a polynomial ring. This leads to a fully algebraic description of the group of 2-string links up to link-homotopy as the dual group associated to $\textrm{Mil}$. As a by-product, we obtain that non repeated Milnor invariants are polynomial maps, and we show that this can be used to give a new proof of their finite type property.

papers.title: Finite generation of the second homology group of the genus three Torelli group
papers.abstract: We prove that the group $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated, where $\mathcal{I}_3$ is the Torelli subgroup of the mapping class group of a closed genus-three surface $\Sigma_3$. A key role in the proof is played by establishing the following property: for each symplectic transvection $t_x\in\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$, we have $$ \bigl(t^{120}_x-1\bigr)^{57}\bigl(t_x^{24}-1\bigr)(t_x-1)^6H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})=0. $$ The proof is based on the study of the spectral sequences associated with the action of $\mathcal{I}_3$ on the Bestvina-Bux-Margalit complex of minimizing cycles and with the actions on certain auxiliary complexes of the stabilizers of two- and three-component multicurves on $\Sigma_3$. The remaining ingredients are Tavgen's theorem, which asserts that $\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$ has bounded elementary generation, and the result of Kassabov and Putman, which asserts that $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated as a $\mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Sp}_6(\mathbb{Z})]$-module.

papers.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
papers.abstract: In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves. The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk. We also prove a Weyl law of the capacities for all toric domains in dimension $2n$. The algebraic verification is based on a chain model for the Chiu-Tamarkin complex of all toric domains in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, which recovers Irie's conjectural chain model of $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology for star-shaped toric domains (defined only) in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

papers.title: Derived sheaves in locally conformally symplectic geometry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use derived sheaves to study rigidity phenomena in the cotangent bundles of manifolds endowed with some locally conformally symplectic ($\frak{lcs}$) structure. Taking inspiration from the work of Guillermou, Kashiwara and Shapira, we define a quantization for ``$\frak{lcs}$'' Hamiltonian isotopies, as well as new quantities: the asymptotic Betti numbers of a sheaf. We then show that those quantities are ``well behaved'' with respect of said quantization and use this to give a sheaf-theoretical proof of the Chantraine-Murphy theorem. We also consider the quantization in light of the Tamarkin morphism and the displacement energy of sheaves. This allows us to derive a non-squeezing theorem for $\frak{lcs}$ geometry that is similar, although not identical, to the one recently proven by Bertelson, Chakravarthy, and Sandon. Indeed, the result shown in this paper is more in line with the contact non-squeezing theorem shown by Eliashberg, Kim and Polterovich in 2006.

papers.title: Categorical structures of Kuranishi spaces with $L_{\infty}[1]$-algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce $L_{\infty}$-Kuranishi spaces by associating, to each chart, $L_{\infty}[1]$-algebras defined on open neighborhoods of points in the zero locus of the Kuranishi section. We show that these objects collectively form a category into which the category of smooth manifolds naturally embeds. Some notions in \cite{FOOO1} are modified to achieve the desired categorical structures; for instance, the tangent bundle condition for chart embeddings is replaced by a quasi-isomorphism condition for the $L_{\infty}[1]$-structures.

papers.title: Learning Transfers: Kan Extensions of Topological Invariants of Learned Representations
papers.abstract: When a learned representation is reused for a new task, which of its structure should survive? A task is a small category, a change of task is a functor $J$, and the invariants of a trained representation form a functor $F$. The left Kan extension $\operatorname{Lan}_JF$ is the invariant that the source and the change of task force on the target: by its universal property, every comparison of the source with an observed target invariant factors through it. The transfer discrepancy is the largest distance, over the target objects, between this extension and the observed invariant. For persistent homology the extension is a cokernel over comma categories, and a functorial version of the discrepancy, which also compares the maps between target objects, is $1$-Lipschitz under interleavings. On finite samples the discrepancy is a bottleneck distance, computed without approximation. For data glued from two pieces whose exclusive parts lie farther apart than the filtration scale, a Mayer-Vietoris sequence identifies what extending homology loses, while extending chains loses nothing. For a merge of labelled point clouds, the degree-zero discrepancy vanishes if and only if some $1$-Lipschitz classifier has a margin above the filtration scale at every sample point. In experiments on sampled manifolds, trained encoders and pretrained image models, every exact prediction holds on every sample. The discrepancy of truncated invariants recovers a hidden merge of separated parts far above chance and tells the intended target of a merge from a permuted control, but across pretrained models it does not track the accuracy of a linear probe.

papers.title: On the internal homotopy theory of the motivic homotopy category
papers.abstract: We develop an $\infty$-categorical framework for internal homotopy theory (truncations, homotopy groups, and Eilenberg-MacLane objects) of an accessible localization of an $\infty$-topos. For the motivic localization over a perfect field $k$, we show that a motivic space has trivial motivic $n$-truncation iff it has trivial Nisnevich $n$-truncation ($n\geq-2$), identifying internal $n$-Eilenberg-MacLane objects with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of groups when $n=1$ and strictly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of abelian groups when $n\geq2$. We further prove that a generically free Nisnevich group sheaf is strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff it is birational (which for the free group sheaf $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ holds iff $A$ is birational), whereas for an \'etale-weakly unramified sheaf of sets $A$, $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ is $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff $A$ is itself $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Non-birational, \'etale-weakly unramified motivic sheaves of sets (such as $\mathbb{G}_m$) thus generate (non-abelian) $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves that are not strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Combining this obstruction with essentially smooth base change, we prove that for a qcqs scheme $S$, $\mathcal{H}^{mot}(S)$ is an $\infty$-topos iff $S=\emptyset$. We also study relative truncation and connectivity under a localization. Over a qcqs scheme $S$, this identifies external $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings with internal motivic $n$-coverings via pullback along the localization unit, yielding a motivic $n$-Galois correspondence over $k$. For connective morphisms over $k$, we establish a higher $\mathbb{A}^1$-Van Kampen theorem and a Nisnevich-local-to-global $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-connectivity criterion; in particular, a $k$-scheme is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected iff it admits a Nisnevich cover by $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected schemes whose pairwise fiber products have $k$-points.

papers.title: Homotopy $n$-types of cubical sets and graphs
papers.abstract: We give a new construction of the model structure on the category of simplicial sets for homotopy $n$-types, originally due to Elvira-Donazar and Hernandez-Paricio, using a right transfer along the coskeleton functor. We observe that an analogous model structure can be constructed on the category of cubical sets, and use it to equip the category of (simple) graphs with a fibration category structure whose weak equivalences are discrete $n$-equivalences.

papers.title: Computer-assisted proofs for the fourth algebraic transfer in certain generic degrees
papers.abstract: This paper restructures the author's earlier article in Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures to correct its erroneous invariant-dimension calculations for the fourth Singer algebraic transfer and is written as a replacement for that article. More precisely, we determine the domain and image of the transfer in the degree families $2^{s+t+1}+2^{s+1}-3$ with $t\ne3$ and $2^{s+t}+2^s-2$ with $t\notin\{2,3,4\}$, where $s,t$ are positive integers. Divided-power spikes are basis elements dual to polynomial monomials whose exponents have the form $2^j-1$ for nonnegative integers $j$. Their translates under ${\rm GL}_4(\mathbb F_2)$, the group of invertible $4\times4$ matrices over the field with two elements, generate submodules of the Steenrod kernel, the subspace annihilated by all positive Steenrod squares. We present these submodules as quotients of sums of permutation modules on complete flags, which are chains in $\mathbb F_2^4$ containing one subspace of each dimension $0,1,2,3,4$. Identifying the relation spaces in these presentations gives explicit equivariant comparison isomorphisms. A recursion obtained by separating even and odd exponents in each variable reduces the comparisons to specified identities of finite-dimensional subspaces. These comparisons apply to both complete degree families, including the parameter values omitted from the transfer theorem. Duplication and partial flag embeddings also give theoretical comparisons in specified parameter ranges. As a consequence, Singer's injectivity conjecture holds in rank four in both degree families under the stated parameter restrictions. The cokernel is one-dimensional in homological degree $256$ and zero in every other degree in those ranges.

papers.title: Revisiting the $\beta_1$-action on the 3-primary stable homotopy groups of spheres
papers.abstract: Let $\beta_1$ be the first 3-torsion class in the stable homotopy groups of spheres in even degree. Toda showed that $\beta_1^5 \neq 0$, whilst $\beta_1^6 = 0$. Shimomura generalised this to the 144-periodic family generated by $\beta_1$, written as $\{\beta_{1+9s}\}_{s\geq 0}$, and showed that any $5$-fold product $\prod_5 \beta_{1+9s} \neq 0$, whilst all 6-fold products $\prod_6 \beta_{1+9s} = 0$. In this article, we give a simple proof of these results as well as some generalisations to other 144-periodic families. Along the way, we also refine known detection results for these families. Our tools include BP-synthetic spectra, and the well-known Adams--Novikov spectral sequence for the spectrum of topological modular forms at the prime $3$ as well as its Adams operations.
